deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Riemann's 1857 memoir on linear differential equations with algebraic coefficients, 'Zwei allgemeine Lehrsätze über lineare Differentialgleichungen mit algebraischen Coefficienten', published posthumously in the Werke (1876). A 'system' (y_1,...,y_n) is an n-tuple of many-valued functions with finitely many branch points a,b,...,g. Under a positive circuit around a it undergoes y -> A y with a constant matrix A. Systems with the same monodromy substitutions A,B,...,G form a 'class'. On the previous page a constant substitution (alpha) brings A to diagonal form: y = alpha z, with z_i -> lambda_i z_i. Each z_i = (x-a)^{mu_i} * (holomorphic and nonzero at a). Here mu_i ≡ log(lambda_i)/(2 pi i) mod Z, and no essential singularities are allowed.

Theorem announced on this page: any n+1 systems y^{(0)}=y, y^{(1)},...,y^{(n)} of the same class satisfy a linear homogeneous relation sum_k a_k(x) y^{(k)} = 0, with polynomial coefficients a_k.

Step 1 (linear algebra). Consider the n equations sum_{k=0}^n a_k y_i^{(k)} = 0, for i=1..n, as n homogeneous equations in n+1 unknowns. The solution is unique up to a factor, provided the n x (n+1) matrix Y=(y_i^{(k)}) has rank n. By Cramer's rule, a_k is proportional to (-1)^k D_k. Here D_k is the n x n minor obtained by deleting the k-th column of Y. The minor named on the page, Sum ± y_1^{(1)} y_2^{(2)} ... y_n^{(n)}, is D_0.

Step 2 (monodromy of the minors). Each column y^{(k)} transforms by the same A, since the systems are in the same class. Hence after the circuit the minor is det(A [y^{(1)} ... y^{(n)}]) = det(A) D_0. Also det A = lambda_1 ... lambda_n.

Step 3 (local expansion). [My filling:] D_0 * (x-a)^{-s}, with s = sum_i log(lambda_i)/(2 pi i), is single-valued near a. D_0 has no essential singularity there. So D_0 = (x-a)^s * (Laurent series with finitely many negative terms), i.e. an expansion in powers of x-a rising by 1.

Step 4 (lowest exponent). Because all systems share A, the same alpha diagonalises all of them: y^{(k)} = alpha z^{(k)}. Then D_0 = det(alpha) * det(z_i^{(k)}). Expand by the Leibniz formula. The term z_1^{(1)} z_2^{(2)} ... z_n^{(n)} equals (x-a)^{mu_1^{(1)} + ... + mu_n^{(n)}} times a function finite and nonzero at a. A general term has lowest exponent sum_i mu_i^{(sigma(i))} for a permutation sigma. [My remark:] all these sums are congruent mod 1, since mu_i^{(k)} ≡ log(lambda_i)/(2 pi i). So the order of D_0 at a is >= mu_bar = min_sigma sum_i mu_i^{(sigma(i))}. It is equal to mu_bar 'in general', since cancellation can only raise it. Analogous minima nu_bar,...,rho_bar are defined at b,...,g.

Continuation on the next page: D_0 (x-a)^{-mu_bar} ... (x-g)^{-rho_bar} is single-valued and finite in the finite plane, with polynomial growth at infinity. By Liouville it is a polynomial of degree <= -(mu_bar+...+rho_bar). The minors therefore have ratios that are polynomials times powers whose exponents differ by integers. Hence the a_k can be taken polynomial.
errors: No real errors. Two tacit assumptions: (i) the n x (n+1) matrix of y's must have rank n, otherwise the minors vanish identically and the proportionality statement is empty (Riemann addresses identically vanishing minors only on the next page); (ii) the reduction y^{(k)} = alpha z^{(k)} with one common alpha needs A diagonalisable with distinct eigenvalues, which Riemann assumed earlier (distinct lambda_i).

'Allgemein zu reden gleich dem kleinsten' is correctly hedged with 'jedenfalls nicht kleiner': equality can fail through cancellation among terms with equal minimal exponent. Only the inequality is used later.

The equality 'z_1^1 ... z_n^n = (x-a)^{mu_1^1+...+mu_n^n} times a nonvanishing function' is precisely 'z_1^1...z_n^n = (x-a)^{...} multiplied by a function finite and nonzero at a'. The page's written form with '=' before (x-a) is an abbreviation, not an error.

results.what: Any n+1 function systems with the same monodromy (same class) satisfy a linear homogeneous relation with polynomial (rational) coefficients
results.modern_name: Rank-n module structure of solutions with given monodromy over C(x) / Riemann's characterisation of Fuchsian systems by monodromy

results.what: Coefficients of a dependency relation proportional to the maximal minors (Cramer's rule)
results.modern_name: Cramer's rule / kernel of an n x (n+1) matrix

results.what: A Wronskian-type determinant of solutions acquires the factor det(A) under a circuit; its local exponent is >= min over permutations of sums of local exponents
results.modern_name: Monodromy of the determinant; local exponent estimate (precursor of the Fuchs relation)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857; Fuchs 1866 for the exponent relation

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of Riemann's 1857 memoir on linear differential equations, printed in his Gesammelte Werke (1876) and well studied. Its content (Cramer's rule plus monodromy of determinants and local exponents) is known as his.
